result:
Everything is final. Here's the report.

**The idea, in one sentence:** It's a pin-art board — a bed of pins on a 3 px lattice — and the minute is the *impression* an unseen pass pressed into it: each digit is a set of my own centre lines whose distance field becomes pin heights, so every stroke is the rounded ridge the pressing tool left with its wall falling away a pin at a time; the hour is a pin dial pressed into the board's middle between the two minute digits, and the seconds are the pass itself — one pin standing proud on the bottom rail where the hand is pressing, creeping right to left across the minute and then coming back heavy to flatten the board and press the new minute in.

**Renders** (all in `.claude/skills/oled-clock/out/`):
- `pinart-ds.png` — the face at 10:09:30
- `pinart-ds-digits.png` — the ten digits alone, in pairs at full size
- `pinart-ds-turn.png` — 12 frames across 10:09:58 (wipe → blank beat → rise)
- `pinart-ds-hour.png` — 12 frames across 10:59:58 (strike → shockwave → new hour)
- `pinart-ds.gif`, `pinart-ds-hour.gif` — 150 frames at 50 fps each
- `pinart-ds-wear.png` — the burn-in map

**check.mjs:** `--design pinart-ds` **PASS** — 20,160 frames checked, worst frame 0.83 ms on SPI 10 MHz (bus allows 1211 fps at 60), no bus overrun, no controller warnings. 17.9% of the glass lit on average; hottest pixel lit 18.7 h/day, 11.0 h/day at full-contrast equivalent → ~2.5 years to half brightness. `frame()` measures 0.33 ms average.

**Honest weakest point:** the **hour dial**. A circle on a 3 px lattice can only ever be twelve snapped pin heads plus a chain of dots between them — it reads as a dial and the hand reads as a hand, but next to the big solid relief digits it is the one element that is *placed* rather than *pressed*, and it is the only part I could not make as confident as the rest. The runner-up is burn-in: the digits are the hero and they are on all day, so 959 pixels are lit more than half the day (the shipped faces sit at 52–328), which is why the orbit is a whole pin a step and night dimming is deep (208 → 30).

Things I changed after looking, that a reviewer might otherwise flag: the transition originally showed the *next* minute for ~0.8 s before the press began (a wrong time — the frame function used "now" as the post-turn minute); the hour strike was inverted and blanked the board; and the rail's tick marks were landing in a Bayer hole, so the seconds track was invisible at some phases.
